# @zakkster/lite-dnd

> Framework-agnostic drag-and-drop primitives that survive DOM reparents.
> useDraggable / useDroppable / useSortable operate on plain Elements, expose
> reactive state as @zakkster/lite-signal signals, and keep a drag alive when the
> dragged node is reordered or removed mid-drag. Zero runtime dependencies.
> Zero per-move JavaScript allocations.

## Install

    npm install @zakkster/lite-dnd @zakkster/lite-signal

- `@zakkster/lite-signal` is a PEER dependency (state is exposed as its signals).
- Browser/DOM runtime. ESM only. Single file `Dnd.js` with `Dnd.d.ts`.

## Public API

    useDraggable(el, opts?) -> { isDragging, position, delta, data, destroy }
    useDroppable(el, opts?) -> { isOver, destroy }
    useSortable(container, opts?) -> { isDragging, order, destroy }
    activeDrag() -> { data, over } | null      // reactive read of the in-flight drag
    class DnDError extends Error { code }       // invalid_target | invalid_options | not_supported

isDragging / position / delta / isOver / order / activeDrag are lite-signal
signal accessors: call them () to read; they track inside effect()/computed().
Every handle has a synchronous, idempotent destroy().

## Options

    useDraggable: { data?, handle?(selector|Element), disabled?(bool|()=>bool),
                    axis?('x'|'y'|'both', default 'both'), threshold?(px, default 4),
                    onStart?(ctx), onMove?(ctx), onEnd?(ctx) }
    useDroppable: { accepts?(string[] of data.type | (data)=>boolean),
                    disabled?(bool|()=>bool), onEnter?(ctx), onLeave?(ctx),
                    onOver?(ctx), onDrop?(data, ctx) }
    useSortable:  { handle?(selector within an item), axis?('x'|'y', default 'y'),
                    threshold?(px, default 4), disabled?(bool|()=>bool),
                    onReorder?(order, { container, item }) }

ctx = { data, x, y, dx, dy, over: Element|null, cancelled: boolean }

## Behavior and gotchas

- Reparent-safe by design: pointermove/up listen on the element's owner WINDOW
  (not the node); drops resolve by live rect hit-test against a droppable
  registry; a drag's identity is its data payload, never an element reference.
- Zero-GC hot path: per pointermove no JS object is allocated by the library.
  position()/delta()/activeDrag() return STABLE references whose fields are
  mutated in place; reactivity is driven by a version-counter signal. Read
  fields synchronously inside an effect (typically via destructuring) and do
  not retain the returned reference across frames. The only platform-mandated
  per-move allocation is DOMRect from getBoundingClientRect.
- onEnter / onLeave are symmetric: every onEnter has a matching onLeave,
  including at drop time (target receives onDrop then onLeave) and on cancel.
- useSortable is MANAGED: it reorders the DOM via native insertBefore during the
  drag. In a virtual-DOM host, use the draggable/droppable primitives and reorder
  your own data instead.
- order is a permutation: order[newIndex] = item's ORIGINAL index at drag start.
  Apply with: next = order.map(i => prev[i]).
- Overlapping droppables: the innermost (smallest-area) rect containing the
  pointer wins.
- threshold distinguishes a click from a drag; below it, no drag starts and
  neither onStart nor onEnd fires.
- The dragged element/item carries a `data-dragging` attribute while active.
- destroy() is idempotent on every handle; calling it during an in-flight drag
  force-stops the drag and fires onEnd with cancelled=true.
- Pairs with @zakkster/lite-element: reordering a list of its components keeps
  each item's internal state (lite-element survives synchronous reparents). No
  dependency on it is required; lite-dnd just uses native DOM moves.
- Out of scope v1: floating drag-image clone, multi-touch, edge auto-scroll,
  keyboard a11y dragging, FLIP animations. Cross-list moves: use draggable +
  droppable.

## Example

    import { useSortable } from "@zakkster/lite-dnd";
    let items = ["a", "b", "c"];
    useSortable(document.querySelector("#list"), {
      handle: ".grip",
      onReorder: (order) => { items = order.map(i => items[i]); },
    });
